RelativeFarguesFontaine.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is in the libraries. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has perfectoid spaces, diamonds, v-sheaves or any Fargues-Fontaine curve, and ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E} do not exist at all; Mathlib's Witt theory is p-typical only. What does exist and is genuinely usable is upstream infrastructure: Mathlib's `WittVector` with Frobenius, Teichmuller lifts, p-adic completeness and the W(k)-is-a-DVR theorem; Fontaine's theta with surjectivity; and an absolute `BDeRhamPlus`/`BDeRham` for a single p-adically complete ring (with principality of ker theta, the theta-extension and the DVR property all still open TODOs in that file). On the geometric side Tau Ceti supplies the entire Huber-ring and adic-spectrum layer RF0 presupposes — Huber pairs, Spa(A,A+) with spectrality, rational subsets and their basis/refinement calculus, completed rational localisation A<T/s> with its integrally closed plus ring (whose openness is not yet proved), and, for the uncompleted localisation A(T/s), the identification of Spa with the rational subset — all sorry-free. Genuinely missing is everything the roadmap names: the ramified Witt algebra and its universal property, 𝒴_S and Y_S, the perfectoidness of the charts and their tilt, sheafiness, the phi-quotient X_S, Div^d and B_D, relative B_dR, O(n) and the graded algebra, and Beauville-Laszlo patching in both its linear and Tannakian forms.

targets.target: Ramified Witt vectors W_{O_E}(R) for a perfect F_q-algebra R and a nonarchimedean local coefficient field E
targets.note: Mathlib has only the p-typical `WittVector p R`, i.e. the case E = Q_p, O_E = Z_p, q = p. There is no O_E-coefficient (ramified) Witt construction anywhere: `grep -rn -i 'ramified witt\|W_\{O_E\}'` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Teichmuller representatives in W_{O_E}(R)
targets.note: `WittVector.teichmuller` is the p-typical Teichmüller map R →* W(R). Mathlib also has the Teichmüller map `Perfection.teichmuller : Perfection (R ⧸ I) p →* R` for any I-adically complete ring with R/I of characteristic p, which gives Teichmüller representatives in W_{O_E}(R) as soon as that π-adically complete ring exists; Tau Ceti's `teichmuller` is the case R = F_q (W_{O_E}(F_q) = O_E), on units. The ramified Witt algebra itself is absent, so the target is partial.

targets.target: Frobenius on W_{O_E}(R) (the q-Frobenius)
targets.note: Mathlib's `WittVector.frobenius` is the p-power Witt Frobenius; `frobeniusEquiv` makes it an isomorphism for a perfect base. The q = p^f Frobenius of a ramified coefficient ring is not constructed.

targets.target: pi-adically complete flat O_E universal property of W_{O_E}
targets.note: In the p-typical case Mathlib proves the ingredients of the universal property except existence: W(k) is p-adically complete (`isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP`) and p-torsion-free (`eq_zero_of_p_mul_eq_zero`), W(k)/p ≅ k (`quotientPEquiv`), and ring maps out of W(R) into a ring where p is nilpotent are determined by their values on Teichmüller lifts (`eq_of_apply_teichmuller_eq`, the uniqueness half). Existence of lifts, and the whole statement for ramified O_E, are missing; `WittVector.lift` is the inverse-limit universal property of truncations.

targets.target: Mixed-characteristic comparison with the completed scalar extension of W(-) over W(F_q)
targets.note: No comparison W_{O_E}(R) = W(R) ⊗_{W(F_q)} O_E (completed) exists; `WittVector/Compare.lean` only compares W(ZMod p) with Z_p.

targets.target: Equal-characteristic identification W_{O_E}(R) = R[[pi]]
targets.note: `PowerSeries R` exists in Mathlib but there is no Witt-vector identification with it; the equal-characteristic case of ramified Witt vectors is not formalised.

targets.target: Functoriality, reduction, topology and uniformizer-change comparisons
targets.note: `WittVector.map` gives functoriality and `WittVector.Complete` gives the p-adic topology, both p-typically. Uniformizer-change comparison has no counterpart because there is no uniformizer parameter.

TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic.summary: Nothing in this roadmap exists in either library, and the gap is unusually clean: 'Berkovich', 'tropicalization' in the geometric sense, 'balancing', 'Baker-Norine', 'Mumford', 'Schottky', 'Tate curve', 'Coleman integration' and 'metrized line bundle' all return zero hits across Mathlib and Tau Ceti. Mathlib's `MinTropical`/`MaxTropical` (formerly `Tropical`) are only the min-plus and max-plus semirings. What is available is adjacent infrastructure of real use: Tau Ceti's complete adic-spectrum layer (Spa(A,A+) with arbitrary-rank valuative points, rational subsets, analytic points, residue-field valuations, the closed polydisc with its classical points), its models of curves over a DVR with finite DVR extensions, its numerical types (the weighted dual graph with vertex genera, the arithmetic-genus formula, and Pic(T) = coker of the weighted intersection matrix, proved of rank one with finite torsion — the combinatorial Jacobian TB.3 wants), its PL/convex-polyhedron and toric-cone machinery, and the full function-field Riemann-Roch theorem. Genuinely missing is every stage's own content: the Berkovich spectrum and its comparison with Spa, the point-type classification and the skeleton metric, analytification and retraction, the graph Laplacian/specialization/slope formula and Baker-Norine, tropicalization with weights and balancing, faithful tropicalization, model metrics and measures, local heights, and Tate/Mumford uniformization with its integration interfaces.

targets.target: The Berkovich spectrum M(A) of a Banach algebra as the set of bounded multiplicative seminorms
targets.note: The word 'Berkovich' does not occur in either library: `grep -rn -i berkovich` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns nothing. Mathlib has the bundled `MulRingSeminorm`/`RingSeminorm` that would be its points, and `contraction_of_isPowMul_of_boundedWrt` (a bounded map into a power-multiplicative seminorm is a contraction), the standard input for boundedness by the norm. `WeakDual.characterSpace` (continuous unital algebra homs with the weak-* topology) is defined over any topological field and is compact for a complete normed algebra over a proper field, ℚ_p included, but it consists of homomorphisms, not seminorms; no seminorm spectrum is formed.

targets.note: Only the character space of a topological algebra carries a weak-* topology in Mathlib; there is no seminorm-valued analogue.

targets.note: Tau Ceti builds the residue ring and the induced valuation on the residue field of a point of Spa (`residueFieldValuation`), which is the adic counterpart; the Berkovich completed residue field H(x) is absent. Mathlib's `spectralNorm` is the norm on an algebraic extension of a nonarchimedean field, a different object.

VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals.summary: The one real library asset is Mathlib's `WittVector.Isocrystal`: a K(p,k)-vector space with a Frobenius-semilinear automorphism, with morphisms, isomorphisms, the standard slope-m object and the Dieudonné-Manin classification proved in dimension one over an algebraically closed field. That is VB0's category and the r = 1 case of its classification, for the coefficient field E = Q_p only - substantial, but no VB0 target is met in the stated generality, so the stage is ranked not built rather than partly built. Tau Ceti adds a Brauer group of central simple algebras with base change and splitting, but no cyclic algebra and no local invariant Br(E) = Q/Z, so VB0's Brauer-invariant obligation stands. Everything else in the roadmap is missing at the level of its carrier: there is no Fargues-Fontaine curve, no perfectoid space, no diamond or v-sheaf, and - strikingly - no semistability or Harder-Narasimhan formalism anywhere in either library, in any setting, so VB1's slope theory, VB2's classification, VB3's Banach-Colmez spaces and VB4's relative HN strata have neither objects nor the general machinery they would specialise.

targets.target: Finite-dimensional spaces over E-breve with a bijective sigma-semilinear operator, their morphisms, and the category of isocrystals
targets.note: Mathlib does have isocrystals: a K(p,k)-vector space with a φ-semilinear automorphism, over the fraction field of W(k) for a perfect integral domain k of characteristic p, together with homomorphisms and isomorphisms. Two things the stage asks for are missing: the coefficient field is E = ℚ_p only (there is no q-Frobenius over a ramified E-breve), and the class carries no finiteness hypothesis, so `finrank = 1` or `Module.Finite` must be added by hand.

targets.note: Mathlib proves the classification only in dimension one: over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, a one-dimensional isocrystal is isomorphic to the standard slope-m object for some m : ℤ. The general finite-dimensional statement, the simple objects of rational (non-integral) slope, the multiplicities, and the Hom and endomorphism division algebras are absent — `grep -rn -i 'dieudonn|isocrystal'` finds nothing beyond this one file.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces.summary: This is by some distance the most-built roadmap in the batch: Tau Ceti carries a ~30000-line, sorry-free development under `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/` and `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/` that covers most of Layers 0-2. Layer 1 is finished - Spv A with its patch presentation and spectrality, the pro-constructible calculus, cofinal ideals and c-Gamma_v(I), Spv(A,I) with the retraction r_I and Lemma 7.5, Cont A with Theorem 7.10 and Corollary 7.12. What is genuinely missing, in order: in Layer 0, the topology and universal property of module-coefficient restricted series, two of the three implications of Wedhorn Theorem 6.16 and the converse of Proposition 6.17, Weierstrass division/preparation and the noetherianity of K<X_1,...,X_n> (so BGR 5.2.6 is unproved and no nondiscrete ring is yet known to be strongly noetherian), the family-indexed topological localisation A(T/S) (only the singleton-denominator case exists) and Wedhorn 6.9(1); in Layer 2, a statement of when Spa(phi) is spectral, Lemma 7.54 for complete non-Tate rings, Proposition 8.2(2) in full and Definition 7.56's affinoid algebras; in Layer 3, openness of A_U+ (so (A_U,A_U+) is not yet a Huber pair), the homeomorphism Spa(A_U,A_U+) = U for the *completed* localisation, which the library states as an open problem, the structure sheaf O_X itself, O_X+, stalks, the category V^pre and the three sheafiness predicates; in Layer 4, flatness of restriction maps between arbitrary rational subsets (only same-denominator numerator enlargements and A -> A<T/s> are proved), Lemmas 8.33/8.34, the Cech statement, preservation of strong noetherianness under completion, stable uniformity and Buzzard-Verberkmoes; the whole of Layer 5's adic-space geometry and gluing; and all of Layer 6 except Mathlib's Witt-vector package. Of the Layer 4 algebra, Remark 8.29, Lemma 8.31 and Corollary 8.32 are done and Proposition 8.30 is proved in those two cases, so Tate acyclicity also waits on the general restriction maps, its last two lemmas and a sheafiness predicate to state the conclusion in.

targets.target: Bounded subsets of a topological ring and their elementary calculus (subsets, finite unions, products, finite sets, images, transport along topological ring isomorphisms)
targets.note: Bounded.lean states the definition exactly as in mathlib4#40013 (the PR the layer asks to coordinate with) and proves subsets, unions, finite sets, finite pointwise products, images and transport. Boundedness is not preserved by an arbitrary continuous map, and the file carries the extra open-at-zero hypothesis the layer asks to be stated separately.

targets.target: A° = power-bounded elements as a subring for nonarchimedean rings, A°° = topologically nilpotent elements as an ideal of A°, and preservation of both under topological ring isomorphisms
targets.note: The subring structure is built from `IsPowerBounded.add_of_commute`/`.mul` under a nonarchimedean additive group, which is Wedhorn Proposition 5.30 in the form the layer insists on (neighbourhood basis by subgroups, not linearly topologised).

targets.target: Huber ring, pair of definition (A₀,I), Tate ring, pseudouniformiser
targets.note: `PairOfDefinition` bundles an open subring with a finitely generated ideal whose adic topology is the subspace topology; `IsHuberRing` asserts one exists; `IsTateRing` asks for a topologically nilpotent unit.

targets.target: Wedhorn Lemma 6.2: the rings of definition are exactly the open bounded subrings
targets.note: The TFAE version adds the intermediate `open + adic for a not-necessarily-finitely-generated ideal`, which is more than the layer asks.

targets.target: Wedhorn Corollary 6.4: intersections and joins of rings of definition are rings of definition, and A° is their union
targets.note: `isPowerBounded_iff_exists_mem_ringOfDefinition` is the `A° = ⋃ A₀` half; 6.4(4) is `exists_pairOfDefinition_le_le`. The file notes that 6.4(2) is deliberately excluded.

targets.target: Wedhorn Lemma 6.6: an ideal is open iff it contains a large power of IA, equivalently IA ⊆ its radical
targets.note: Both forms are proved; `IsTateRing.isOpen_iff_eq_top` records the Tate corollary the layer uses later (a nonzero Tate ring has no proper open ideal).

targets.target: Every Huber ring is nonarchimedean; A° is open and integrally closed in A; every open integrally closed subring contains A°°
targets.note: All four statements are present with exactly the stated hypotheses.

targets.target: In a Tate ring, high powers of a pseudouniformiser lie in a given ring of definition and ϖⁿA₀ is a neighbourhood basis of zero
targets.note: Stated for a fixed pair of definition and then existentially for a Tate ring.

targets.target: Rings of integral elements A⁺ ⊆ A°, Huber pairs and continuous morphisms of pairs
targets.note: `Pair.Hom` carries a continuous ring map preserving the plus rings, with identity/composition laws; `Pair.quotient` and `Pair.Hom.quotientLift` give the quotient pair and its universal property.

targets.target: Completion: A → Â has dense image, kernel closure{0}, is a topological embedding when A is Hausdorff; Â is Huber (Remark 6.8) and the Tate property is preserved; base change of Proposition 6.9(1)
targets.note: The Huber and Tate structure on Â is constructed with an explicit pair of definition; the dense-image and embedding statements are Mathlib's general completion facts. What I could not find anywhere is Wedhorn Proposition 6.9(1), the base-change statement the layer asks to be recorded separately: grepping `6\.9` over the whole Huber tree returns nothing.

targets.target: Weighted restricted power series A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩_T with its topology, functoriality, density of polynomials (5.49) and the power-bounded universal property (5.50)
targets.note: `IsWeightFamily` is exactly Wedhorn's standing hypothesis (Tᵢ^m·U a neighbourhood of 0), which the layer insists on; `weightedMap` with `weightedMap_id`/`weightedMap_comp` gives functoriality and `dense_weightedPolynomials` is 5.49.

targets.target: Topological localisation A(T/S) of Proposition and Definition 5.51 for a family T = (Tᵢ) of numerator bundles and denominators S = (sᵢ) indexed by the same I, with its universal property, the separated completion A⟨T/S⟩, and independence of auxiliary choices
targets.note: Everything is built, with full universal properties over complete Hausdorff targets, for the singleton-I case: `locSubring P T s S` takes a `Finset A` of numerators and a single denominator `s` with `IsLocalization.Away s S`. The I-indexed family version the layer states (numerators bundled per denominator) is not constructed; `LocalizationTopology/Pi.lean` only assembles the product map A → ∏_{t∈T} A⟨T/t⟩, not a localisation at a family.

targets.target: Restricted series with coefficients in a complete topological module; substitution and evaluation; quotient and iteration isomorphisms A⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩ ≅ A⟨X,Y⟩; compatibility with completed tensoring by a finitely generated module
targets.note: The ring-level package is built: the iteration isomorphism A⟨X⟩⟨Y⟩ ≅ A⟨X,Y⟩ of topological rings, evaluation and substitution (WeightedEval), completeness, and Remark 8.29, M ⊗_A A⟨X⟩ ≅ M⟨X⟩ for finitely generated M (`restrictedMvPowerSeriesBaseChange_bijective`). The module-coefficient series M⟨X⟩ of the roadmap's first milestone exist only as a submodule (`restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule`, with functoriality): neither their topology nor their universal property is constructed. Quotient isomorphisms exist only for the Laurent-type quotients and along open quotient maps.

targets.target: Weierstrass division and preparation over a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field
targets.note: Mathlib has Weierstrass division and preparation for formal power series over a complete local ring (`PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassDivision`, `exists_isWeierstrassFactorization`, and an I-adic division theorem in the same file). Nothing covers the Tate algebra K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ over a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field: `grep -rn -i weierstrass` over the Huber tree returns nothing.

targets.target: Noetherianity of K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ for a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field K, and the conclusion from BGR 5.2.6 that every such K is strongly noetherian
targets.note: The predicate exists, but its own docstring says `every complete rank-one nonarchimedean field satisfies it (BGR 5.2.6 — not yet formalised)`. The only witnesses supplied are the discrete case (`IsStronglyNoetherian.of_discreteTopology`) and transport results; no nondiscrete Tate ring is proved strongly noetherian anywhere.

targets.target: Definition of strongly noetherian, its zero-variable readings, and stability of noetherianity under quotients and the iteration
targets.note: Stated for a nonarchimedean ring rather than only a Tate ring, so more general than the layer. `of_surjective` needs a countably generated nhds 0, which the layer does not mention but which the file argues is load-bearing.

targets.target: Henkel's open mapping theorem and Wedhorn Theorem 6.16, Propositions 6.17–6.18: a continuous surjective linear map between completely metrisable modules over a complete Hausdorff Tate ring is open and induces the quotient topology
targets.note: Henkel's theorem is proved abstractly from a zero sequence of units and specialised to Tate rings (`IsTateRing.hasZeroSequenceOfUnits`), giving the form used later: a continuous surjective linear map between complete first-countable Hausdorff modules over a complete Hausdorff Tate ring is open and a quotient map. Proposition 6.18 is proved in full: (1) finite modules carry a complete Hausdorff module topology (`completeSpace_moduleTopology`, `IsTateRing.t2Space_moduleTopology`) and it is the only such topology (`IsTateRing.isModuleTopology`); (2) linear maps between finite modules over a complete noetherian Tate ring are strict (`LinearMap.isStrictMap_of_module_finite`); `IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`, which still assumes a closed range, is only related and is no longer cited. What is missing is the rest of Theorem 6.16 — only '(a) N complete and (b) u surjective imply (c) u open' is proved, not the other two implications — and the converse of Proposition 6.17: only 'noetherian ⇒ every submodule closed' (`isClosed_of_isNoetherian`) exists.

targets.target: Examples: a discrete ring is Huber; ℤ_p is Huber but not Tate; ℚ_p and F⸨t⸩ are Tate; ℚ_p⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ is complete and strongly noetherian
targets.note: Four of the five examples are proved exactly. Completeness of ℚ_p⟨T⟩ follows from `completeSpace_weightedRestrictedSubring_one_weight`, but its strong noetherianness is exactly the missing BGR 5.2.6 input, so that example is not finished.

duplicates.note: R0 assumes this layer's Huber/Tate algebra and adds completed tensor products; it restates strong noetherianness as a hypothesis on the affinoid products it glues, so the strongly-noetherian vocabulary is shared but the constructions are not.

A0 names AdicSpacesPartII as canonical owner and restates the same topological-algebra contract (rings of definition, ideals of definition, plus rings by integral closure, pseudouniformiser tracking) as its supplier interface.

targets.target: Spv A as valuative relations on A, basic opens Spv(A)(f/s), support, pullback along ring maps, lifts through quotients and localisations
targets.note: Points are `ValuativeRel` instances on A, so a point carries no chosen value group, which is the representation the roadmap asks for. `localization_comap_isEmbedding` upgrades the localisation lift to a topological embedding.

targets.target: The continuous support map supp : Spv A → Spec A and its section by trivial valuations (Remark 4.6)
targets.note: Continuity of `suppFun` and surjectivity via the section are both proved.

targets.target: Spectrality of Spv A via the boolean-table embedding into {0,1}^{A×A}, closedness of the image, Tychonoff compactness of the constructible topology, clopen basic opens, T0, and the reusable criterion of Proposition 3.31
targets.note: `instance : SpectralSpace (Spv A)` is at PatchPresentation.lean:225 and `instance : T0Space (Spv A)` at ValuationSpectrum.lean:200; the reusable patch criterion lives in `TauCeti/Topology/Spectral/PatchCriterion.lean`, exactly the Proposition 3.31 factorisation the layer asks for.

targets.target: Pro-constructible subsets of a spectral space: intersections, inverse images along spectral maps, products, and spectrality of a pro-constructible subspace
targets.note: A complete reusable calculus: empty/univ, binary and indexed unions and intersections, compact and closed sets, preimages, products, and the passage to `CompactSpace`, `PrespectralSpace`, `QuasiSober` and `SpectralSpace` on the subspace.

targets.target: Cofinality theory of Lemmas 7.1–7.2, the convex subgroup cΓ_v(I) of Definition 7.3, and Lemma 7.4
targets.note: cΓ_v(I) is `characteristicSubgroupOfIdeal`, characterised as the greatest convex subgroup at which I is cofinal; the last declaration is Lemma 7.4 in the form a consumer checks.

targets.target: Spv(A,I) for an f-adic A and an ideal with a finitely generated ideal of the same radical, the retraction r_I, Lemma 7.5 (spectrality and spectrality of r_I), and Remark 7.6
targets.note: Remark 7.6 is respected throughout: the files state explicitly that spectrality is proved on the subspace, by the witness topology coinduced along r_I, because the inclusion into Spv A is not spectral.

targets.target: Cont A for a Huber ring, Theorem 7.10 (Cont A = {v ∈ Spv(A,IA) : v(a) < 1 for a ∈ I}), Corollary 7.12 (closed, hence spectral), independence of the pair of definition, and vertical/horizontal specialisation as needed
targets.note: `cont` is defined with no pair of definition in sight, so independence of the pair is automatic rather than a theorem. Vertical generization is `Valuation.Coarsen`/`Microbial` and the horizontal side is the monotonicity of `r_I` in `CofinalIdeal/Restrict.lean:407`; both are developed only as far as Theorem 7.10 and the analytic-point theory need, which is what the layer asks.

duplicates.note: D0 asks for the same constructible/pro-constructible calculus, generalization, spectral maps and limits of spectral spaces; `TauCeti/Topology/Spectral/ProConstructible.lean` already discharges the pro-constructible half of that stage.
A4 wants invariance of the valuation spectrum under uniform completion, which consumes exactly this layer's Spv/Cont API rather than rebuilding it.

targets.target: Spa(A,A⁺) = {v ∈ Cont A : v(a) ≤ 1 for a ∈ A⁺} with the subspace topology, and Theorem 7.35 (pro-constructible in Spv(A,IA), hence spectral)
targets.note: Stated for an arbitrary `Subring A` as plus ring, so more general than Wedhorn's ring of integral elements; the `SpectralSpace (spa Aplus)` instance is at Spa/Spectral.lean:90. Both inputs are proved on the Spv(A,IA) side, since the inclusion into Spv A is not spectral.

targets.target: The contravariant continuous map on adic spectra induced by a morphism of Huber pairs, with the hypotheses under which it is spectral
targets.note: Continuity and contravariant functoriality are proved (`spaComap`, `Pair.Hom.spaComap`), together with the preimage formula for rational subsets and the closed embedding for quotient pairs. The roadmap also asks for 'the exact hypotheses under which this map is spectral': no statement that `spaComap` is a spectral map exists (the only `IsSpectralMap` results in the AdicSpace tree concern the retraction r_I).

targets.target: Rational subsets R(T/s) under the open-ideal condition, the five parts of Remark 7.30 including finite intersections, and the basis of quasi-compact opens
targets.note: Remark 7.30(5) is proved in the binary form and, as the layer's Theorem 7.35 proof needs, in the finite form with no nonemptiness hypothesis. The `T ↦ T ∪ {s}` normalisation is `rationalSubset_insert_self`.

targets.target: Proposition 7.34 (rational subsets are unchanged by small perturbations of their defining functions)
targets.note: Proved over an arbitrary Huber ring, dropping Wedhorn's complete Hausdorff hypothesis: perturbing numerators and denominator inside a power of the ideal of definition, or inside a neighbourhood of zero, leaves the rational subset unchanged, which is the roadmap's formulation. Wedhorn's statement also concludes that the perturbed numerators generate an open ideal; that clause is not proved, and it can fail without completeness, so the declarations generalise the set equality but not the whole proposition.

targets.target: Corollary 7.53 (T generates the unit ideal iff the standard family (R(T/t))_{t∈T} covers Spa(A,A⁺)) over a complete Hausdorff affinoid ring
targets.note: The forward direction needs no hypothesis on A at all; completeness enters only in the converse, through the support criterion.

targets.target: Lemma 7.54: over a complete affinoid ring every open cover has a standard rational refinement
targets.note: The roadmap states Lemma 7.54 for complete A. It is proved for a complete Hausdorff Tate ring, for arbitrary open covers (`…_of_isTateRing`), and for any Huber ring only for covers by rational subsets whose numerator sets generate the unit ideal (Refinement.lean:141). Over a non-Tate ring the numerator ideals of rational subsets need only be open, so the general complete case is not covered.

targets.target: Wedhorn Remark 7.55, the descending chain of rational subsets adjoining one numerator at a time
targets.note: Proved without Wedhorn's invertibility and strictness assumptions on the dominating element; the consumer supplies the unit from Corollary 7.32 if it has one.

targets.target: Proposition 8.2(2): a rational subset of a rational subset is rational in the original adic spectrum
targets.note: Only the denominator-clearing half is proved: a rational subset over the localisation is the pullback of one presented by elements of A. The file says explicitly that obtaining 8.2(2) in full still needs an admissible finite presentation in A and the passage from A(T/s) to the completed A⟨T/s⟩.

targets.target: Proposition 7.52(1) (A⁺ is the sub-unit locus of Spa(A,A⁺), no completeness hypothesis) and 7.52(2) (the complete-case unit criterion), stated separately
targets.note: 7.52(1) (`mem_iff_forall_vle_one`) uses only openness and integral closedness of the plus ring, as the layer demands. 7.52(2) is `isUnit_iff_forall_mem_spa_notMem_supp` (Spa/Support.lean:144) for a complete Hausdorff Huber pair, via Proposition 7.51 (`exists_mem_spa_supp_eq_of_isMaximal`, `exists_mem_spa_le_supp_of_ne_top`). The engine is Wedhorn Proposition 7.18(1), proved in full. The earlier Points.lean variant `isUnit_of_forall_not_vle_zero` assumes every maximal ideal is open, which its own docstring notes is vacuous for nonzero Tate rings.

targets.target: Proposition 7.49(1): Spa(A,A⁺) = ∅ ↔ A/closure{0} = 0, with the Hausdorff form kept separate
targets.note: The Hausdorff specialisation is a separate declaration, as the layer asks; it is stated under `T2Space`, not `CompleteSpace`.

targets.target: Analytic points (Definition 7.39), the analytic locus, its openness, Proposition 7.49(2) with the emptiness criterion, behaviour under the separated quotient, and the cover by rational subsets with Tate coordinate rings
targets.note: `isTateRing_completion_locTopology_of_mem_generators` (Analytic.lean:305) is the statement that the chart rings of that cover are Tate, and `spaAnalytic_eq_spa_of_isTateRing` is Remark 7.40(3), that every point of a Tate affinoid is analytic. The separated-quotient half of 7.49(2) is in Spa/SeparationQuotient.lean.

targets.target: Quotient Huber pairs and Proposition 7.38: the adic spectrum of A/J is a closed subspace of Spa(A,A⁺) with the expected universal property
targets.note: The universal property is at the pair level (`quotientLift`, `quotientLift_unique`) and the closed embedding with its range description at the spectrum level.

targets.target: Affinoid algebras over a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field (Definition 7.56), closed polydiscs from K⟨T₁,…,Tₙ⟩ with plus ring A°, and the elementary points and rational subdomains of the closed unit disc (Example 7.57)
targets.note: The closed polydisc Spa(A⟨T⟩, A⟨T⟩°) and its classical points are built over an arbitrary complete nonarchimedean base, more general than Definition 7.56's field. 'Quotient of a restricted power-series algebra' exists as `IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType`, but Definition 7.56's class of affinoid algebras over a complete rank-one field is not singled out, and Example 7.57's classification of the non-classical points and rational subdomains of the closed unit disc is missing.

duplicates.note: P2 asks for the tilting homeomorphism of valuation spectra and its rational-subset correspondence: it presupposes this layer's rational-subset calculus and transports it across the tilt, rather than reproving it.
A1 builds the small étale and finite étale sites on top of the rational basis and keeps higher-rank field pairs (K,K⁺), i.e. this layer's arbitrary-rank Spa points, as a standing requirement.
TB.0 asks for the comparison between a strictly affinoid algebra and its Huber adic spectrum, so it restates Spa(A,A⁺) and its rank-one points as the object being compared with M(A).
A0 asks to construct the analytic locus and the Tate charts on which its fibre-product constructions are applied, restating this layer's analytic points and their Tate cover (T10).

targets.target: The coordinate ring A_U = A⟨T/s⟩ of a rational subset with its topological universal property (s invertible, every t/s power-bounded)
targets.note: Both the algebraic universal property and Wedhorn's geometric Lemma 8.1 form (Spa(φ) factors through R(T/s)) are proved, the latter with the unit condition derived rather than assumed.

targets.target: A_U⁺ as the integral closure of the image of A⁺[T/s], and that (A_U,A_U⁺) is a Huber pair
targets.note: Integral closedness and containment in the power-bounded subring are proved, so A_U⁺ satisfies two of the three conditions of a ring of integral elements. Openness of A_U⁺ in A⟨T/s⟩ is not proved (LocalizationTopology/Plus.lean: 'Openness is still not proved here'; Spa/Localization/PresentationIndependence.lean: 'not proved anywhere on main'), and `IsRingOfIntegralElements` has an `isOpen` field, so (A_U, A_U⁺) is not yet shown to be a Huber pair. Before completion all three conditions hold (`isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure_adjoin_plus`).

targets.target: The natural homeomorphism Spa(A_U,A_U⁺) ≅ U, identifying valuations and rational subsets
targets.note: The homeomorphism is proved for the *uncompleted* topological localisation A(T/s), not for A⟨T/s⟩: Localization/Homeomorph.lean says the completed case `requires a further extension of continuous valuations along the dense completion map and is intentionally not identified here`, and Localization/Basic.lean records the same gap. So the layer's stated homeomorphism is not yet available.

targets.target: Canonical isomorphisms between the localisations of two presentations of the same rational subset, compatibility for three presentations, and restriction maps with identity and composition laws
targets.note: Presentation independence is proved only under two hypotheses Wedhorn does not carry — invertibility of each denominator in the other presentation's coordinate ring and openness of the plus subrings — and the module says so outright. The identity/composition laws exist for the presentation-indexed restriction maps.

targets.target: CompleteSeparatedTopCommRingCat with products and equalizers, created by the forgetful functor to TopCommRingCat
targets.note: `Limits.lean` proves `HasLimits` for the category and the `IsClosedUnderLimitsOfShape` instances for discrete shapes and parallel pairs, from which `CreatesLimitsOfShape` for the inclusion follows by synthesis; the equalizer argument is exactly the closed-subring-of-a-complete-separated-ring one the layer describes.

targets.target: The structure presheaf 𝒪_X on the rational basis with 𝒪_X(U) = A_U, extended to all opens by the limit over rational subsets, agreeing on rational subsets
targets.note: The limit presheaf exists and lands in CompleteSeparatedTopCommRingCat, but it is indexed by *presentations*, not by rational subsets, and the module states explicitly that it is `not identified with Wedhorn's 𝒪_X` — that identification waits on the presentation-independence isomorphisms above. So the value on a rational subset is not yet known to be A_U.

targets.target: 𝒪_X⁺(U) = {f : v_x(f_x) ≤ 1 for all x ∈ U}
targets.note: The evaluation map a section would be tested through is built (the residue-field valuation of a point), and its docstring names this as its purpose, but no plus subpresheaf is defined; grepping for `𝒪_X⁺`/`plusPresheaf` across the library returns only that docstring.

targets.target: Stalks: every stalk is a local ring, the support of the point valuation is its maximal ideal, and the valuation factors through the residue field
targets.note: Nothing about stalks exists: `grep -rn -i stalk` over TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace and TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber returns nothing, and there is no structure sheaf whose stalks could be taken. What exists is the ring-level factorisation of a point's valuation through κ(v) = (supp v).ResidueField of A itself (`residueFieldValuation`), which a stalk statement would use.

targets.target: The category 𝒱^pre of pre-adic spaces (space, presheaf of complete separated topological rings, local stalks, residue-field valuations) with its morphisms, affinoid pre-adic spaces, and 𝒱
targets.note: Nothing of the sort exists: there is no PresheafedSpace-style carrier anywhere in TauCeti (`grep PresheafedSpace` returns nothing) and no pre-adic space structure.

targets.target: Huber.IsSheafyPair, Huber.IsSheafyRing (Definition 8.26), Huber.IsStablySheafyRing, their implications and invariance under completion and isomorphism
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'IsSheafyPair|IsSheafyRing|IsStablySheafy'` over both libraries returns nothing; none of the three predicates is defined.

targets.target: 𝒪_X(X) ≅ A as a topological ring for a complete Hausdorff pair
targets.note: Trivial.lean proves the underlying computation — at denominator 1 the localisation topology is the topology A already carries, so A⟨T/1⟩ is the Hausdorff completion of A and the structure map is an isomorphism of topological rings when A is complete Hausdorff. Its own header says this is the Layer 3.5 target `at the level of the localisation construction the presheaf is built from`, i.e. not yet a statement about 𝒪_X, which does not exist.

targets.target: The basis sheaf criterion: rational subsets are a basis closed under finite intersections and quasi-compact, every cover of a rational subset has a finite rational refinement, the sheaf condition on the basis is equivalent to the sheaf condition on all opens, and the equalizer topology is the subspace topology
targets.note: Every clause is present once the right declarations are cited. Rational subsets form a basis closed under finite intersections (Basis.lean:255/197) and are quasi-compact (`isCompact_of_mem_spaRationalFamily`, any Huber ring). Every cover of a rational subset by opens has a finite rational refinement (`exists_finite_spaRationalFamily_refinement`, any Huber ring). Lemma 7.54 (Refinement.lean:168, dropped from the citations) is only the Tate special case for covers of the whole space. review.notes: Checked all 243 targets of the 36 layers against the roadmap extracts and, for AdicSpaces Layers 0 and 2, Wedhorn's text. All 342 original citations (256 distinct) resolve at their file and line in declarations.tsv and the pinned sources; none is private, and no cited file contains a sorry outside comments (the AdicSpace/Huber trees, about 30,000 lines, are sorry-free). One citation was a deprecated alias (Mathlib `Tropical`, now `MinTropical`) and was replaced. Every presence and partial claim was re-read at source with its variable lines and hypotheses; every absent target was re-searched by concept over declarations.tsv and both source trees, except two with no standard name (TB.1 descent, TB.3 specialization inequality). Status changes (11 targets): six present targets are only partial — AdicSpaces L0 module-coefficient restricted series (no topology or universal property) and Theorem 6.16/Proposition 6.17 (one implication and one direction only), L2 spectrality of Spa(phi) and Lemma 7.54 for complete non-Tate rings, L3 the Huber pair (A_U, A_U+) (openness of A_U+ unproved), L4 Proposition 8.30 (only same-denominator enlargements and A -> A<T/s>); L3's basis sheaf criterion becomes 'both' with Mathlib's comparison lemma; TB.0's rank-one comparison goes from absent to partial (Wedhorn Remark 7.42(2)); three partial targets with nothing stated become absent (L3 stalks, TB.2 refinement compatibility, VB0 Brauer invariant). Several citations were wrong or missing: the audit cited a Tate-only Lemma 7.54 for the rational-subset refinement clause, a vacuous-on-Tate-rings 7.52(2), and a rational-localisation theorem as 'completion preserves strong noetherianness'. Five notes made false absence claims (Mathlib's power-series Weierstrass preparation, Weil and Néron–Tate heights, DivisibleHull, the multiplicative Torsor class, the scheme pro-étale site), and the RelativeFarguesFontaine summary credited the completed localisation with results proved only for the uncompleted one. Duplicates: all 101 resolve to live, non-retired stages. 22 were removed, being consumers or prerequisites (by their own notes), stages of the same roadmap that depend on each other, or wrong layers. 29 missed owners were added, among them Tau Ceti's StableReduction Layers 1, 3 and 6, ClassFieldTheory Layer 5, AnalyticToricGeometry Layer 0, BunGAndNewtonStrata BG1 and BG2:uniformization, and FarguesFontaineDiamonds F1, F2 and F4. No layer verdict changes: 29 not built, 6 partly built, 1 built (AdicSpaces Layer 1, confirmed target by target). The audit's overall picture — AdicSpaces Layers 0-2 largely built in Tau Ceti, nothing of Berkovich, tropical, relative Fargues–Fontaine or Banach–Colmez theory in either library — stands.
